title: Same chord, different layout
summary: C, E and G in any order, at any height, are still a C chord.

steps.title: Voicing
steps.body:
C E G, E G C and G C E are all a C major chord: the same three notes, laid out differently. The way a chord's notes are arranged, which is lowest, which on top, how spread out, is its **voicing**.

**Why it matters:** Band keyboard players rarely play every chord from its root. Choosing voicings is how they sound smooth and stay out of the bass player's and singer's way.

steps.title: Three voicings of C
steps.body: Close together from C, close together from E, and spread over two octaves.

items.prompt: Play C, E and G together, in any order.
Now play E, G and C together, with E lowest.

steps.title: Spread it out
steps.body: Play C with your left hand and E and G high up with your right. Then try G at the bottom. Same chord, new colours.

items.prompt: Play an F major triad, with the notes in any order.
